questoes.pergunta:
Scenario: Vértice Telecom, a fiber and mobile carrier with 4 million subscribers, built a support resolution agent with the Claude Agent SDK that serves customers through its app and WhatsApp. Through internal MCP servers, the agent uses the tools get_customer, lookup_invoice, run_line_diagnostics, check_outage, issue_credit, and escalate_to_human. Goal: resolve at least 70% of billing and connectivity tickets on first contact. Constraints: no account changes before verifying the account holder's identity; credits above R$ 200 require approval from a human analyst; every interaction generates a protocol number required by Anatel, which must be correctly communicated to the customer.

In production, the agent loop ends the interaction whenever the model's response contains a text block. In several tickets, the response included the text "I'll test your line now" along with a tool_use block for run_line_diagnostics, and the customer never got a reply. What is the appropriate fix?
opcoes: Instruct the model in the system prompt never to write text in the same response in which it calls a tool, so that the presence of text once again signals the end of the interaction.
Detect intent phrases in the text such as "I'll test" or "I'll check" and, when they appear, keep the loop open even if the response contains text.
Decide based on stop_reason: on "tool_use", execute the tools and send back the tool_result blocks; end only on "end_turn".
Always end after a fixed number of iterations, such as 8.
questoes.explicacao: The agentic loop is driven by stop_reason: "tool_use" means execute and continue; "end_turn" means finish. The content can mix text and tool_use.
feedbacks: Tempting because it seems to address the cause, but it depends on probabilistic model behavior and keeps the anti-pattern of deciding loop termination by content rather than by stop_reason.
Classic anti-pattern: parsing natural language to decide control flow. Fragile (other phrasings slip through) and unnecessary, since stop_reason conveys exactly that.
Correct. stop_reason is the official continuation signal. Text and tool_use can come together in the same response; having text does not mean the turn is over.
An iteration cap serves as a safety backstop, not as the primary stopping mechanism: it cuts off legitimately long interactions and prolongs short ones.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, the rule is to verify the account holder's identity before any account change. Today this exists only in the system prompt, and an audit found that about 3% of credits granted via issue_credit had no prior verification. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Rewrite the system prompt instruction prominently, with few-shot examples of interactions in which verification is done before the credit.
Create a PreToolUse hook that denies issue_credit as long as the session state does not record identity verification.
Only allow issue_credit when the model states confidence above 0.9 in the verification.
Add a second agent that reads the entire conversation before each credit and approves or rejects the call based on what was said.
questoes.explicacao: A critical prerequisite (identity before account changes) belongs in code: a PreToolUse hook with permissionDecision "deny" until the prerequisite is satisfied.
feedbacks: Tempting because it usually reduces the error rate, but the prompt is still probabilistic. For a financial rule, "reducing" is not enough: the exam expects enforcement in code.
Correct. A rule with financial and security consequences requires deterministic enforcement. The PreToolUse hook blocks the call before it happens, with a zero failure rate.
Self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated; a model that skipped verification tends to report high confidence. It is not a deterministic control.
More complex and still probabilistic: it trades a cheap deterministic check (a state flag) for another error-prone LLM judgment.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, credits above R$ 200 require approval from a human analyst, and analysts complain that when they receive a case, they have to ask the customer all the questions again. Which TWO measures make up the correct design? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Put "never grant credits above R$ 200" in the system prompt as the sole safeguard, since the rule is easy to understand.
A PreToolUse hook that inspects the amount field of issue_credit and, above R$ 200, denies the call with a reason that directs the agent to escalate the case.
Allow the agent itself to grant credits above R$ 200 when the customer shows high dissatisfaction, to avoid churn.
Escalate via escalate_to_human with a structured summary: customer and line, problem, diagnostics already run, amount requested, reason for the block, and recommended action.
When escalating, attach the complete raw transcript of the conversation, without a summary, so the analyst has all available context.
questoes.explicacao: Financial limit → hook that blocks in code; handoff → structured summary with what the human needs to make a decision.
feedbacks: A simple rule does not become deterministic just because it is simple: a prompt has a non-zero failure rate, which is unacceptable for a financial limit.
Correct. The limit is financial and must be enforced in code, by inspecting the tool input before execution.
Uses sentiment as an exception criterion, and also circumvents a financial control. Sentiment is not an approval-authority criterion.
Correct. The analyst usually does not read the transcript; the handoff needs a structured summary so they can act without redoing the interaction.
Tempting because it seems "complete", but it is exactly what causes rework: the human has to dig through the transcript. The correct handoff is structured.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, the model started emitting two tool_use blocks in a single response: run_line_diagnostics and lookup_invoice. The application executes both and sends each tool_result in a separate user message; since then, subsequent requests fail or the model ignores one of the results. What should be done?
opcoes: Return both tool_result blocks in a single user message, each with the tool_use_id of the corresponding block.
Set disable_parallel_tool_use: true permanently, so that the model requests only one tool at a time and the current code works again.
Send the results in the order they finished, one user message per result, adding text that says which tool each one refers to.
Respond only to the first tool_use and discard the second; if the model still needs the invoice, it will request lookup_invoice again on the next turn.
questoes.explicacao: Multiple tool_use blocks in one response → execute all of them and return all the tool_result blocks in a single user message, matched by tool_use_id.
feedbacks: Correct. In parallel tool use, all results go back together in a single user message, each linked to its tool_use_id; a failed result is sent too, with is_error: true.
Works as a workaround, but sacrifices the latency gains of parallelism to hide a client-side bug. The fix is to build the message the way the API expects.
Keeps the structural error: correlation is done by tool_use_id, not by explanatory text, and the results from a single response go in one message.
Every tool_use needs a corresponding tool_result; leaving one unanswered causes an error and wastes a call the model has already decided to make.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, two tickets arrive at the same time. Customer 1, very angry, is cursing at support over a duplicate R$ 9.90 charge for an add-on service, a case in which the policy provides for an automatic refund. Customer 2, calm and polite, asks for a waiver of the early termination fee because they moved to an address without fiber coverage, a situation the policy does not cover. How should the agent act?
opcoes: Escalate customer 1's ticket because of the very negative sentiment and resolve customer 2's by charging the fee as the contract stipulates.
Escalate both: negative sentiment and an exception request are both triggers.
Ask the model for a 0-to-10 confidence score on each case and escalate automatically whenever the score is below 7.
Resolve customer 1's ticket with the policy refund and escalate customer 2's, which requests an exception the policy does not cover.
questoes.explicacao: Escalate on an explicit request for a human, a policy gap/exception, or lack of progress; not on sentiment or self-reported confidence.
feedbacks: Inverts the criteria: it escalates based on sentiment (anti-pattern) and handles on its own an exception the policy does not cover.
Strong sentiment is not an escalation trigger. Escalating the trivial case wastes analysts and works against the first-contact resolution goal.
Self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated and does not capture the real criterion (policy gap, explicit request for a human, lack of progress).
Correct. Sentiment is not complexity: the angry case is simple and covered by the policy; the calm case involves a policy gap, a legitimate escalation trigger.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, in long interactions (40+ turns), the history is summarized automatically. After summarization, the agent started giving out Anatel protocol numbers with transposed digits and rounded invoice amounts. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Migrate to a model with a larger context window so that summarization becomes unnecessary in most interactions.
Summarize the history more often, every 10 turns, so that each summary covers less information and loses fewer details.
Add the instruction "pay special attention to numbers and protocol numbers when summarizing the conversation" to the system prompt.
Keep a persistent "case facts" block (protocol number, line, amounts, dates) that is never summarized.
questoes.explicacao: Summarization loses exact values, IDs, and dates. Fix: a persistent case facts block, kept outside the summary.
feedbacks: Treats the symptom: a larger window costs more per turn, worsens lost in the middle, and does not guarantee that exact values survive when summarization does happen.
More summaries mean more opportunities for paraphrasing; the problem is structural (summaries don't preserve exact values), not a matter of frequency.
A vague, probabilistic instruction; it does not guarantee verbatim preservation. The expected pattern is to separate critical facts from summarizable text.
Correct. Summaries lose precisely the exact values, IDs, and dates; a case facts block preserves what cannot be paraphrased.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, a customer identifies themselves only as "Maria Souza" and asks for a copy of their bill. get_customer returns three account holders with that name, and currently the agent simply proceeds with the first result. What should the agent do?
opcoes: Choose the record with the most recent activity, which is statistically the most likely to be the person making contact.
Escalate the interaction to a human, since the identity ambiguity indicates that the agent cannot resolve the case.
Ask the customer for an additional identifier (CPF or line number) to disambiguate before accessing any billing data.
Show the customer the three records found, with address and line, so they can indicate which one is theirs.
questoes.explicacao: Multiple customers in the search → ask for an identifier to disambiguate; don't guess and don't expose third-party data.
feedbacks: Guessing with a heuristic risks exposing another account holder's data (a privacy problem) and acting on the wrong account.
Unnecessary escalation: the agent resolves the ambiguity with a simple question. It is neither a policy gap nor a lack of progress.
Correct. With several possible matches, the agent should ask for an identifier that disambiguates, never pick a record by heuristic.
Resolves the ambiguity, but leaks personal data of the other two account holders to an unverified user (LGPD).

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, when the billing system is down, lookup_invoice catches the timeout and returns an empty list with a success status. The agent then tells the customer that "there are no outstanding invoices". How should the tool behave?
opcoes: Keep the empty list, but instruct the agent in the system prompt never to claim there are no invoices and to always suggest the customer check the app.
Return the string "Operation failed" so that the model realizes something went wrong and apologizes to the customer.
Return a structured error (transient category, isRetryable: true, attempted action), distinguishing failure from "nothing found".
Make the tool retry the call indefinitely until billing is back up, so it never returns an incomplete result to the agent.
questoes.explicacao: An error must not be silenced as an empty success. Timeout = structured, retryable transient error; empty = information.
feedbacks: The silent suppression continues: the agent doesn't know when a real failure occurred and starts doubting even legitimate empty responses.
Better than lying, but it's the generic-error anti-pattern: with no category and no indication of retryability, the agent doesn't know whether to retry, wait, or escalate.
Correct. Empty ≠ failure: an empty list with success means "the search ran and found nothing". A timeout means the search did not run and should arrive as a structured, retryable error.
Unbounded retries stall the interaction and hide the failure. A transient error calls for retries with backoff and a limit, followed by a structured error.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, the agent frequently calls run_line_diagnostics when there is a regional outage (it should use check_outage), and vice versa. Both tools have the same description: "Checks the customer's connection problems". What is the first fix to make?
opcoes: Rewrite both descriptions, explaining each one's purpose, when to use it, and how it differs from the other.
Train an intent classifier that decides, ahead of the agent, which of the two tools should be called for each message.
Use tool_choice to force check_outage as the first call in every connectivity ticket.
Remove check_outage and have run_line_diagnostics also query regional outages internally, keeping the current description.
questoes.explicacao: Overlapping tools with nearly identical descriptions → rewrite the descriptions to differentiate purpose and usage (or rename/merge them with a clear description).
feedbacks: Correct. The description is the tool selection criterion; nearly identical descriptions cause misrouting. It is the simplest fix that solves the problem.
A more complex solution than necessary: the cause is the ambiguous description. A routing classifier comes after the simple fix has been exhausted.
Encodes a decision tree outside the model and wastes calls unnecessarily; it does not fix the ambiguity of the descriptions.
Merging tools can be valid, but if the description stays vague, the selection problem just moves elsewhere; the primary fix is the description.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, issue_credit rejects a credit because the customer has reached the policy's monthly credit limit, and returns only the text "Error while processing". The agent tries the same call four more times before giving up. Which error response would solve the problem?
opcoes: {"isError": true, "errorCategory": "transient", "isRetryable": true, "retry_after_seconds": 30, "message": "Failed to process credit"}
{"isError": true, "message": "Error while processing. Please try again later."}
{"isError": true, "errorCategory": "business", "isRetryable": false, "message": "Monthly credit limit reached"}
{"success": true, "credited": 0, "message": "No credit applied"}
questoes.explicacao: Business error → errorCategory "business", isRetryable false, a clear message: the agent explains the policy or escalates, without retrying.
feedbacks: Wrong category: classifying a policy rule as transient encourages exactly the useless retries you want to eliminate.
Still generic and even suggests a retry; without a category and isRetryable, the agent cannot distinguish a policy rule from instability.
Correct. A business error is not retryable; the category and isRetryable: false tell the agent to stop trying and to explain the policy or escalate.
Masks the rejection as success, leading the agent to tell the customer that "everything is fine". This is silent suppression.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, the system prompt says "escalate to a human when appropriate". An analysis of 500 interactions shows inconsistent escalation: identical cases are sometimes escalated and sometimes not. Which change to the prompt brings the most consistency?
opcoes: Replace it with explicit criteria: what counts as a trigger, what does not, and examples of borderline cases.
Add "be conservative and, when in doubt, escalate", to reduce the risk of the agent resolving on its own what it shouldn't.
Lower the temperature to make escalation more deterministic.
Ask the model to explain, before responding, whether it considers the case complex, and escalate when it judges that it is.
questoes.explicacao: Explicit criteria (what counts, what doesn't, borderline examples) beat vague instructions like "when appropriate".
feedbacks: Correct. Vague instructions like "when appropriate" produce inconsistency; explicit criteria covering what counts, what doesn't, and borderline examples make the judgment reproducible.
Still vague ("when in doubt") and pushes behavior toward over-escalation, without resolving the inconsistency.
Targets the wrong symptom: the inconsistency comes from the lack of criteria, not from sampling. Moreover, on recent models, sampling parameters may not even be accepted.
Keeps the judgment without defined criteria; "complex" is as vague as "appropriate".

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, the agent classifies the customer's initial intent as "cancellation", "number portability", or "plan downgrade", and frequently gets it wrong on ambiguous messages like "I want to pay less, or I'm switching to another carrier". Which TWO changes improve the classification? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Include 40 examples of the most common case ("I want to cancel") so that the model has plenty of evidence of the expected format.
Add "use good judgment to correctly classify ambiguous messages" to the end of the prompt.
Include 3 or 4 varied few-shot examples, focused on ambiguous cases like this one, each with the message, the classification, and the reasoning that led to it.
Ask the model to also return its confidence in the classification and discard classifications below 0.8.
Explicitly define each category, stating what counts and what does not (e.g., asking for a cheaper plan without mentioning leaving = downgrade).
questoes.explicacao: Few-shot with 2 to 4 varied examples that include reasoning + explicit criteria per category are the levers for ambiguous cases.
feedbacks: Many examples of the easy case don't teach the boundary and encourage memorization; effective few-shot means a few varied examples that cover the edges.
"Use good judgment" is exactly the kind of vague instruction that produces inconsistency.
Correct. Few-shot targeted at borderline cases, with explicit reasoning, teaches the decision pattern and generalizes better.
Self-reported confidence is not calibrated; discarding does not fix the misclassification in ambiguous cases.
Correct. Explicit criteria per category eliminate the free interpretation that causes errors in ambiguous cases.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, an engineer proposes hard-coding the fixed sequence "diagnostics → invoice → credit" in the orchestrator for every ticket, forcing each step's tool via tool_choice, because "the agent sometimes picks a different order". Interactions vary widely (some are billing-only, others connectivity-only). What is the best assessment?
opcoes: Approve the fixed sequence, because deterministic flows are always more reliable than letting the model decide the order of the tools.
Reject it: let the model choose the tools in the loop and enforce in code only the critical prerequisites.
Approve the sequence, but only for connectivity tickets, and leave billing tickets to the model choosing freely.
Keep the loop free and list the preferred tool order in the prompt.
questoes.explicacao: The model decides the flow within the loop; deterministic code (hooks/prerequisites) only for critical rules.
feedbacks: Confuses enforcing a critical rule with scripting the entire flow. Forcing diagnostics on a billing-only ticket wastes calls and worsens the experience.
Correct. In the agentic loop, the model decides which tool to use and when to stop; code enforces only the critical rules. An external decision tree straitjackets variable cases.
Still encodes a decision tree outside the model and requires classifying the ticket beforehand, without addressing the real concern (critical prerequisites).
If the order isn't critical, it doesn't need to be enforced; if some step is critical (identity), a prompt isn't enough. It's a halfway solution.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, a response occasionally arrives with HTTP 200, stop_reason "refusal", and content without the expected text. The code reads content[0].text, gets an empty value, and sends the customer a blank message, logging the interaction as successful. What is the fix?
opcoes: Treat as errors only responses with an HTTP status other than 200 and apply automatic retries in those cases.
Check whether content[0].text is empty and, if so, resend the same request until text comes back.
Check stop_reason before reading the content and treat "refusal" as a distinct outcome, with a fallback.
Increase max_tokens, since empty content usually indicates that the response was cut off before the text was generated.
questoes.explicacao: stop_reason "refusal" comes with HTTP 200; check stop_reason before consuming the content.
feedbacks: Doesn't catch the problem: the refusal comes with HTTP 200. Checking only the HTTP status is exactly the bug described.
A fragile heuristic that ignores the signaled cause (stop_reason) and may endlessly repeat a request that will be refused again.
Correct. A refusal arrives with HTTP 200; only stop_reason distinguishes it from success. Code that ignores stop_reason treats a refusal as an empty success.
Truncation due to the output limit shows up as stop_reason "max_tokens", not "refusal"; raising the limit changes nothing here.

questoes.pergunta: At Vértice Telecom, the get_customer result includes the full CPF and the card details on file, which end up in the model's context and in the conversation logs, violating the LGPD policy. The agent only needs the last 3 digits of the CPF to confirm identity. What is the most appropriate solution?
opcoes: A PostToolUse hook that masks the CPF and card data in the get_customer result.
Instruct the model in the system prompt never to repeat the CPF or card data in its replies to the customer.
A PreToolUse hook that blocks get_customer whenever the conversation mentions payment data.
Ask the model, after each get_customer call, to summarize the result while discarding the sensitive fields.
questoes.explicacao: PostToolUse is the place to normalize/mask tool results (e.g., PII) before they reach the model.
feedbacks: Correct. PostToolUse deterministically normalizes and sanitizes tool results before the model (and the conversation logs) see them.
The data has already entered the context and the logs; at most, the instruction protects the reply, and only probabilistically.
Blocks the wrong tool at the wrong time: the problem lies in the content of the result, not in the decision to call the tool.
The model has already read the sensitive data, and the summary is probabilistic. The sanitization needs to happen earlier, in code.

questoes.pergunta:
Scenario: Lumen Saúde, a healthtech company that supports hospital pharmacy committees, operates a multi-agent system that produces evidence dossiers on therapies (for example, "efficacy of GLP-1 agonists in adolescents with obesity"). A coordinator agent, built with the Claude Agent SDK, delegates to specialized subagents: scientific literature search (via an MCP server for a bibliographic database), web search, clinical trial registry analysis, and synthesis/writing. Goal: deliver, within a few hours, a dossier that a physician can audit. Constraints: every claim needs a traceable source, disagreements between studies must remain visible, and the system must not fill gaps with uncited knowledge.

The coordinator delegates to the literature subagent with the prompt "Research the studies relevant to the user's question". The subagent returns generic studies on obesity in adults. What is the most likely cause, and the fix?
opcoes: The subagent has too many tools available; simply reducing the tool set will make it focus on the right question and stop returning generic results.

The subagent has an isolated context and does not see the original question; the coordinator must explicitly pass in the prompt the question, population, time period, inclusion criteria, and expected output format.
The subagent should be created with access to the coordinator's full history; configure it to inherit the conversation by default.
The subagent's model is too weak for the task; switching to a larger model will fix the interpretation of the question.
questoes.explicacao: The subagent's context is isolated: the delegation must explicitly carry the question, the constraints, and the output format.
feedbacks: Reducing tools improves tool selection, but doesn't give the subagent the information it never received: the question.
Correct. Subagents do not inherit the coordinator's history: everything they need goes explicitly in the delegation prompt.

Tempting (forks do inherit context), but for a well-scoped task the right approach is an explicit, well-specified prompt; inheriting everything consumes context and is no substitute for specifying what you want.
No model can guess a question that isn't in its context; switching models targets the wrong symptom.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the literature, web, and clinical trial subagents are independent of one another, but the log shows the coordinator issuing one Agent tool call per turn, waiting for each result before the next. The dossier takes three times as long as expected. What should change?
opcoes: The coordinator should issue the three Agent tool calls in the same response, so that the subagents run in parallel.
Merge the three subagents into a single subagent with all the tools, eliminating the need for multiple delegations.
Configure the subagents so that each one calls the next directly when it finishes, forming a chain that bypasses the coordinator.
Reduce the subagents' max_tokens so that each one finishes faster and the total time drops.
questoes.explicacao: To parallelize, the coordinator issues multiple Agent calls in the same response.
feedbacks: Correct. Subagent parallelism happens when multiple Agent calls go out in the same response; separate turns mean sequential execution.
Eliminates specialization and inflates the agent's tool count (worse selection), without gaining any parallelism.
Still sequential, and it also breaks hub-and-spoke: subagents should not communicate directly.
Cuts responses off midway (truncation) and does not address the cause: sequential execution.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, for the question "non-pharmacological interventions for insomnia in older adults", the dossier covered only cognitive behavioral therapy; physical exercise, sleep hygiene, and mindfulness were left out, even though the subagents ran without errors. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Increase the number of articles the literature subagent returns per search from 20 to 100, so that less-cited subareas also show up.
Ask the synthesis subagent to fill in the missing subareas with the model's general knowledge.
Add a review subagent at the end that rejects dossiers that are too short.
Decompose more broadly, check coverage of the subareas, and run a second round targeted at the gaps.
questoes.explicacao: Overly narrow decomposition is a D1 anti-pattern: decompose broadly, verify coverage, and run a round targeted at the gaps.
feedbacks: More results from the same narrow search bring more of the same; the gap lies in the decomposition, not in the volume.
Violates the constraint against filling gaps without a source and increases the risk of hallucination in a clinical context.
Detects the symptom (a thin dossier) late and without saying what is missing; it neither fixes the decomposition nor guides the new search.
Correct. This is the overly narrow decomposition anti-pattern; the fix is to decompose broadly, check coverage, and refine iteratively.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, to reduce latency, an engineer proposes that the web search subagent send its findings directly to the synthesis subagent, bypassing the coordinator. What is the best assessment of this proposal?
opcoes: Approve it: direct communication between subagents is the recommended way to reduce latency in multi-agent pipelines.
Approve it, provided that the synthesis subagent logs everything it received directly from the web search.
Reject it and, instead, merge the web search and synthesis subagents into one, eliminating the data handoff between them.
Reject it: in hub-and-spoke, the coordinator routes all communication, evaluates gaps, and handles errors before synthesis.
questoes.explicacao: Hub-and-spoke: the coordinator decomposes, delegates, routes all communication, aggregates, and handles errors.
feedbacks: Gains little latency and loses the central point of control (errors, gaps, re-delegation).
Logging helps with auditing after the fact, but does not give the coordinator back runtime control over gaps and errors.
Eliminates the data handoff, but mixes distinct responsibilities, loses specialization, and the coordinator still doesn't evaluate the findings before synthesis.
Correct. Subagents talking directly to each other is an anti-pattern: the coordinator loses the big picture and the ability to verify coverage and handle failures.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the coordinator invokes all four subagents (literature, web, clinical trials, and synthesis) for every query, including simple questions such as "what is the maximum daily dose approved on the label for drug X?". Cost and time have skyrocketed. What should be done?
opcoes: Keep the full pipeline, but switch the subagents to smaller, cheaper models.
Instruct the coordinator to invoke only the subagents each query needs, with clear criteria for when to use each one.
Create a separate system, outside the coordinator, just for simple questions, with a classifier deciding which system to send each one to.
Cache all the responses and reuse them whenever a similar query comes up.
questoes.explicacao: Invoke only the subagents the query needs.
feedbacks: Reduces the unit cost, but keeps the structural waste of calling subagents the question doesn't require.
Correct. The coordinator should invoke only the necessary subagents; running everything through the entire pipeline is wasteful.
More complex than necessary: deciding which subagents to invoke is already the coordinator's job.
May help with exact repeats, but doesn't fix the design that invokes every subagent for every new question.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, after a refactoring, the coordinator started answering everything on its own and no longer delegates; the logs show no attempt to call subagents. Which TWO configuration checks are the most relevant? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Confirm that the Agent tool (formerly called Task) is in the coordinator's allowedTools.
Confirm that each subagent has access to the coordinator's full conversation history.
Confirm that the coordinator's max_tokens is high enough to fit the subagents' responses.
Confirm that the subagents are defined (e.g., via AgentDefinition) with descriptions that make clear when each one should be used.
Confirm that the subagents use the same model as the coordinator, since different models prevent delegation.
questoes.explicacao: Delegation requires the Agent tool in allowedTools and well-defined subagents, with descriptions that say when to use them.
feedbacks: Correct. Without the Agent tool enabled, the coordinator has no way to create subagents.
Subagents have an isolated context by design; that would not prevent delegation.
Affects the size of the response, not the ability to decide to delegate; the symptom would be truncation, not a complete absence of delegation.
Correct. A subagent's description guides the decision to delegate, just as a tool's description guides tool selection.
Subagents can use different models; that does not block the call.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the bibliographic database (MCP) started returning 429 (rate limit) during peaks. Today the literature subagent passes the raw error on to the coordinator, which aborts the entire dossier. What is the appropriate handling?
opcoes: Local retry with backoff in the subagent; if it persists, a structured error with partial results to the coordinator, which carries on and notes the gap.
The coordinator should abort the dossier whenever any subagent fails, so as not to deliver an incomplete or potentially biased document to a physician.
The subagent should return an empty list when it receives a 429, so that the coordinator continues without interruption.
The coordinator should immediately redo the entire delegation to the subagent whenever it receives the 429, until it succeeds.
questoes.explicacao: The subagent recovers from transient errors locally with backoff and propagates only what it could not resolve, as a structured error; the coordinator continues with the partial results.
feedbacks: Correct. Transient errors are recovered locally; only what could not be resolved is propagated, with context. You don't abort the whole workflow over one step.
Aborting everything over one step is an anti-pattern; a dossier with the gap noted is more useful and more honest than nothing.
Silent suppression: the dossier would then claim there are no studies, when the search never even ran.
Retrying without backoff or a limit worsens the rate limiting and delays everything; recovery from transient errors belongs in the subagent, with backoff.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the web search subagent has accumulated 16 tools (search, fetch, PDF parser, statistics, citation formatting, translation, deduplication, etc.) and has started choosing the wrong tools frequently, even after the descriptions were improved. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Rewrite the descriptions once more, this time with input examples for each of the 16 tools.
Use tool_choice to force the correct tool at each step of the subagent.
Split it into specialized subagents, each with 4 or 5 tools.
Increase the effort of the subagent's model.
questoes.explicacao: Too many tools in one agent degrade selection; split into specialized subagents with 4 to 5 tools each.
feedbacks: The descriptions have already been improved without success; with too many tools in a single agent, improving the descriptions alone is not enough.
Requires someone on the outside to know the right step and tool: it is an external decision tree that takes the choice away from the model.
Correct. With many tools in a single agent, selection degrades; the guideline is a few visible tools per agent, with specialization.
May help marginally, but does not address the structural cause (too many tools in one agent).

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the clinical trials MCP server exposes only tools. Before each analysis, the subagent makes dozens of exploratory calls ("list databases", "list tables", "describe table") to discover what exists. Which change to the server best reduces these calls?
opcoes: Expose the catalog of databases and tables as MCP resources.
Expose the catalog as an MCP prompt.
Use sampling so that the server asks the model to describe the existing tables.
Combine the three exploratory tools into a single explore_everything tool that returns the entire schema at once.
questoes.explicacao: MCP server primitives: tools (actions), resources (read-only content/catalogs), prompts (templates).
feedbacks: Correct. Resources are the primitive for read-only content and browsable catalogs, avoiding blind exploratory calls.
MCP prompts are interaction templates, not the primitive for exposing read-only data.
Sampling is the server requesting a completion from the client; it does not expose data, and the model does not know the server's tables.
Reduces calls, but dumps a huge result into the context on every use; a resource is the mechanism designed for this.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, two meta-analyses of similar quality report reductions of 12% and 8% in an outcome. The synthesis subagent wrote "the therapy reduces the outcome by about 10%". How should the dossier present this?
opcoes: Keep the 10% average, but cite both meta-analyses as sources, since it represents the body of evidence well.
Choose the most recent meta-analysis and report only its value, since newer studies tend to be more reliable.
Omit the outcome, as it is not conclusive.
Present both values with their respective sources and flag the finding as contested.
questoes.explicacao: Conflict between sources: show the values with their sources and label the finding as contested. No averaging and no silent picking.
feedbacks: The average is a number that no source reported; citing both does not make the calculation legitimate.
Silently picking one value hides the disagreement the physician needs to see.
Omitting it erases relevant evidence; the correct approach is to show the conflict, labeled.
Correct. When sources conflict, record the diverging values with their sources; don't silently pick one or average them.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the dossiers come out with several claims that lack an identifiable source. Investigating, the team discovers that the subagents return free-flowing prose summaries to the coordinator. Which change best preserves provenance all the way to the final dossier?
opcoes: Ask the synthesis subagent, at the end, to search the web for a source for each claim that was left without a citation.
Subagents return structured output: each claim with its evidence, source (DOI/URL), and date.
Instruct the subagents to include the phrase "according to the literature" in their prose before each claim.
Send the synthesis subagent the full texts of all the articles read, so that it can cite them directly.
questoes.explicacao: Provenance: a claim → source map with structured metadata, passed between the agents.
feedbacks: Inverts the logic: finding a source after writing the claim is rationalization, not tracing its origin.
Correct. Separating content from metadata (claim, evidence, source, date) lets the attribution survive the aggregation and synthesis steps.
Does not identify the specific source; a physician cannot audit "according to the literature".
Blows up the context (lost in the middle and cost) and does not guarantee the claim → source mapping.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, a study with 2018 data reports a prevalence of 8%, and a survey with 2024 data reports 11% in the same population. The system flagged the two numbers as a "contradiction between sources". What is the correct treatment?
opcoes: Keep the contradiction flag, since any diverging values for the same metric should be flagged as contested.
Record the reference period of each data point and present them as measurements taken at different points in time.
Discard the 2018 study as outdated and report only 11%.
Compute the 9.5% average and report it as the estimated prevalence for the period.
questoes.explicacao: Temporal data: record the reference period; values from different periods are not a contradiction.
feedbacks: Applies the conflict rule mechanically, ignoring the temporal dimension; it confuses the physician.
Correct. Numbers from different periods are not a contradiction; recording the "data as of", publication, and collection dates allows them to be presented as a trend.
Loses trend information and discards valid evidence unnecessarily.
Mixes different periods into a number that no source reported.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the synthesis subagent fills in a JSON with the field evidence_level (enum: "high", "moderate", "low"). When the study does not report its methodological design, the model chooses "moderate" anyway. Which schema adjustment is the most appropriate?
opcoes: Enable strict: true on the tool schema to guarantee that the field always contains one of the three valid enum values.
Remove the field from the schema and ask for the level of evidence to be described in free text in the summary.
Instruct the model to choose "low" whenever it is in doubt, since it is the most conservative option.
Add an "undetermined" value to the enum (or make the field nullable) for when the source does not report it.
questoes.explicacao: A schema whose enum has no way out forces a guess; use "undetermined"/"other" or a nullable field for missing data.
feedbacks: strict guarantees conformance with the schema, which is already being respected. Conformance is not semantic correctness: the guess is still valid under the schema.
Loses the structure that enables filtering and validation; free text brings back inconsistent formats.
Swaps one guess for another: "low" also asserts something the source does not support.
Correct. When the enum has no way out for "I don't know", the model is pushed to guess; an "undetermined" value or a nullable field gives it an honest option.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, after drafting the dossier, the synthesis subagent itself receives, in the same session, the request "review the dossier and point out problems". It almost always approves the text, but physicians find overstated claims. What is the best change?
opcoes: Review with an independent instance, in a fresh context, with explicit review criteria.
Ask the same subagent to review the dossier three times in a row in the same session, to increase the chance of catching errors.
Instruct the synthesis subagent to "be more critical" in the review.
Eliminate the automated review and route every dossier to a full review by a physician before it is sent.
questoes.explicacao: Self-review in the same session is an anti-pattern; use an independent instance with explicit criteria.
feedbacks: Correct. Whoever generated the content carries the bias of its own reasoning; a review in an independent session with explicit criteria finds what the author does not question.
Repeating the self-review repeats the bias; the same session keeps defending its own decisions.
A vague instruction does not remove the bias from the reasoning context.
Removes the cheap automated layer; human review is valuable, but the exam expects you to first fix the design of the automated review.

questoes.pergunta: At Lumen Saúde, the literature subagent receives the instruction "include only high-quality studies" and applies the filter inconsistently: it includes preprints in one round and excludes small randomized trials in another. Which TWO changes make the screening more consistent? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Ask the subagent to assign each study a quality score from 0 to 10 and include those scoring above 7.
Replace "high quality" with explicit criteria: what is included (e.g., a peer-reviewed randomized trial or systematic review) and what is not (e.g., preprints, case reports).
Add "be rigorous and conservative in the selection" to the current instruction.
Run the screening three times and include only the studies approved in every round.
Include 2 or 3 examples of borderline cases (e.g., a randomized trial with n = 40), each with the decision and the reasoning.
questoes.explicacao: Explicit criteria + borderline few-shot with reasoning = consistent judgment.
feedbacks: Swaps one vague judgment for an equally criterion-free numeric one; the score is not calibrated.
Correct. Explicit criteria about what counts and what doesn't eliminate the free interpretation of "high quality".
Yet another vague adjective; the inconsistency remains.
Costs three times as much and entrenches the same lack of criteria; borderline studies still fall randomly on either side.
Correct. Few-shot targeted at the ambiguous cases, with reasoning, teaches where the boundary lies.

questoes.pergunta:
Scenario: Atlas Seguros maintains a .NET monorepo of about 2 million lines (quoting, policy issuance, claims, and actuarial calculation) and is adopting Claude Code for its 80 developers. The platform team has connected internal MCP servers (Jira, a knowledge base, and a read-only staging database) and wants to speed up onboarding and day-to-day tasks. Constraints: no secrets may go into the repository, production data is inaccessible (LGPD), and the team's conventions must apply to everyone without interfering with each developer's personal preferences.

A newly hired developer asks Claude Code: "explain how the premium for an auto insurance policy is calculated". Which codebase exploration strategy is the most appropriate?
opcoes: Use Read on every file in the quoting and actuarial calculation projects before answering, to get a complete view of the flow and not leave out any rule.
Use Glob to list all the .cs files in the repository and decide from their names which ones are relevant.
Ask the knowledge base via MCP for the calculation documentation and answer based on it alone, without looking at the code.
Grep for the entry points (e.g., CalculatePremium), read those files, and follow the references with Grep, reading only what is necessary.
questoes.explicacao: Codebase exploration: grep for the entry points, read, follow references with grep, read. Don't read everything up front.
feedbacks: The read-everything-up-front anti-pattern: it blows through the context in a monorepo this size and degrades the quality of the answer.
Glob helps find files by name pattern, but on its own it doesn't show where the logic lives; names are misleading and the list is huge.
Documentation may be outdated; to explain the actual behavior, the source of truth is the code.
Correct. Incremental exploration: grep for the entry points → read → follow the imports → read. It spends context only on what matters.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, a developer needs to (1) find all files whose name ends in "Calculator.cs" and (2) find all calls to the ApplyLoyaltyDiscount method. Which TWO built-in tool choices are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Glob with the pattern **/*Calculator.cs for task 1.
Grep for the text "Calculator.cs" for task 1.
Grep for the text ApplyLoyaltyDiscount for task 2.
Glob with the pattern **/*ApplyLoyaltyDiscount* for task 2.
Read on every .cs file in the quoting project for task 2.
questoes.explicacao: Glob = files by name pattern; Grep = content inside files.
feedbacks: Correct. Glob finds files by name/path pattern.
Grep searches within file contents; it would find mentions of the name (e.g., in a .csproj), not the files themselves.
Correct. Grep searches the content inside files, which is what you want in order to locate calls to a method.
Glob looks at file names, not content; a method does not appear in the name of the file that calls it.
Reading file by file is expensive and slow; Grep solves it directly.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, Claude Code tries to use Edit to change the line "return total;" at the end of the CalculateDeductible method, but the tool fails because that snippet appears six times in the file. What is the correct way to proceed?
opcoes: Use replace_all to replace all six occurrences of "return total;" with the new line.
Expand old_string with neighboring lines (e.g., the method signature) until the snippet is unique.
Use Bash with sed to replace the first occurrence of "return total;" in the file.
Recreate the file from scratch with Write, typing the content based on what the model remembers of it.
questoes.explicacao: Edit requires a unique snippet: expand the snippet's context, or read the entire file and rewrite it.
feedbacks: Also changes the other five methods, introducing bugs where nobody asked for a change.
Correct. Edit replaces an exact, unique snippet; by expanding the context, the target becomes unambiguous (alternatively, read the file and rewrite it).
The first occurrence is probably not the one in CalculateDeductible; it is a blind edit, with no guarantee of hitting the right spot.
Rewriting from memory, without having read the entire file, risks losing code; rewriting is only safe after reading the complete file.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, the team added the remote Jira MCP server to .mcp.json like this: {"mcpServers": {"jira": {"url": "https://mcp.atlas.internal/jira"}}}. Claude Code cannot connect, and the error suggests that it tried to start a local process. What is the likely cause?
opcoes: The .mcp.json file accepts only local servers; remote servers must be added in the user scope.
The command field is missing, pointing to an executable that bridges HTTP to the remote server.
Remote servers must use SSE; simply change the URL to the /sse endpoint.
"type": "http" is missing; without type, the entry is treated as a stdio server.
questoes.explicacao: In .mcp.json, a remote server needs "type": "http"; without type, the entry is treated as stdio.
feedbacks: False: the project scope (.mcp.json) accepts remote servers normally.
command is for stdio servers; for a remote server, the correct approach is to declare the HTTP transport, not to create a local bridge.
SSE is legacy; the recommended remote transport is Streamable HTTP. The cause is the missing type, not the transport itself.
Correct. A classic trap: a remote entry with url but no type is interpreted as stdio. Always declare the type on a remote server.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, a developer put the Jira API token as a literal value in the headers field of .mcp.json, which is version-controlled. The security team requested a fix. Which TWO approaches are appropriate? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Keep the token in .mcp.json and add the file to .gitignore.
Reference an environment variable in the file, such as "Authorization": "Bearer ${JIRA_TOKEN}", defined on each developer's machine.
Use a headersHelper that fetches a short-lived credential from the secrets vault at runtime.
Encode the token in Base64 in .mcp.json so that it is not readable.
Move the token to the project's CLAUDE.md, from which Claude Code reads it when the session starts.
questoes.explicacao: Secrets in .mcp.json: ${VAR} (with an optional default) or headersHelper for a short-lived credential; never literals.
feedbacks: Ignoring .mcp.json breaks the sharing of the configuration with the team, which is the reason the project scope exists; and the token has already leaked into the history.
Correct. ${VAR} expansion keeps the secret out of the version-controlled file.
Correct. headersHelper generates headers dynamically (e.g., a short-lived token), with no secret in the repository.
Base64 is not encryption; the secret is still in the repository.
CLAUDE.md is version-controlled and enters the model's context; it is an even worse place for secrets.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, the tests are scattered (Quoting/Tests, Claims/Tests, Issuance/Tests, and others yet to be created), and they must all follow the same conventions (xUnit, the AAA pattern, policy builders). Today there is a copy of these rules in each folder's CLAUDE.md, and the copies have already diverged. What is the best solution?
opcoes: Move the conventions to the root CLAUDE.md.
Keep the per-folder CLAUDE.md files and create a CI script that checks whether the copies are identical.
A file in .claude/rules/ with paths: **/Tests/**/*.cs containing the conventions.
Create a /test-conventions skill and ask the developers to invoke it whenever they are going to write tests.
questoes.explicacao: A convention that cuts across directories → a file in .claude/rules/ with paths: (glob).
feedbacks: It works, but it takes up context in every session, even when no one is touching tests; the path-scoped rule is more precise.
Treats the symptom (divergence) and keeps the duplication; new folders still require manual copying.
Correct. A path-scoped rule covers all the test directories (including future ones) from a single file, loading only when files matching the glob are touched.
Depends on remembering to invoke it; a convention that should always apply should not be optional.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, a developer added to the project's CLAUDE.md: "always respond in Spanish" and "use my sandbox at https://sbx-rafael.atlas.internal". His colleagues started getting responses in Spanish and tests pointing to his sandbox. Where should each preference go? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Both in the project's CLAUDE.md, with the comment "for Rafael only".
Both in the organization's managed policy, to ensure they are always applied.
The language preference, which applies to all of his projects, in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (user memory).
The sandbox URL, which is personal and specific to this project, in CLAUDE.local.md at the project root (outside version control).
The sandbox URL in .claude/rules/sandbox.md without frontmatter, so that it loads only when needed.
questoes.explicacao: Hierarchy: user (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) for global personal preferences; CLAUDE.local.md for personal preferences within a project; the project's CLAUDE.md for the team.
feedbacks: The file is loaded for everyone; the model has no way to apply instructions to just one person based on a comment.
Managed policy is for organization-wide rules, not individual preferences; it would affect all 80 developers.
Correct. A personal preference that applies in any project goes in the user's CLAUDE.md, which is not version-controlled.
Correct. CLAUDE.local.md is the place for personal preferences within a project, without affecting the team.
A rule without paths: loads at the start of every session and lives in .claude/, which is version-controlled; it would affect the whole team.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, the team needs to migrate serialization from Newtonsoft.Json to System.Text.Json across about 60 files, with custom converters and more than one possible strategy for handling dates and enums. How should this be carried out in Claude Code?
opcoes: Use plan mode: explore, propose the approach, and edit only after the team approves the plan.
Run it directly in acceptEdits mode, so that the edits to the 60 files are applied without interruption.
Ask Claude to migrate one file at a time with direct execution, reviewing each diff, with no prior planning.
Run it in bypassPermissions on a separate branch, since everything can be discarded later if it goes wrong.
questoes.explicacao: Plan mode for large, multi-file changes involving architectural decisions; direct execution for small, obvious fixes.
feedbacks: Correct. A multi-file change involving an architectural decision and several valid approaches is the classic case for plan mode.
Edits before aligning on the approach; with several valid strategies, the risk of rework across 60 files is high.
Reviewing each diff helps, but without deciding on the strategy first, different files tend to receive inconsistent solutions.
bypassPermissions is not routine for a long, non-contained task, and it does not solve the lack of alignment on the approach.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, the team created the skill .claude/skills/new-endpoint/SKILL.md, which generates the controller, DTOs, validations, and tests. Developers complain that when they are merely discussing an existing endpoint, Claude loads the skill on its own and starts creating files. The skill should run only when someone types /new-endpoint. Which adjustment solves this?
opcoes: Remove the description field from the frontmatter so that the model doesn't know when the skill applies.
Set user-invocable: false in the skill's frontmatter.
Move the skill to .claude/commands/new-endpoint.md, since commands are not loaded automatically.
Add disable-model-invocation: true to the skill's frontmatter.
questoes.explicacao: In the skill's frontmatter, disable-model-invocation: true prevents auto-loading and makes the skill manual-only.
feedbacks: A hack: description is what drives auto-loading and also documents the skill; without it, the skill goes undocumented and the control remains implicit.
Does the opposite: it removes the skill from the user's menu and lets only the model invoke it.
Commands have been merged into skills; invocation control is done through the frontmatter, not the directory.
Correct. disable-model-invocation prevents the model from auto-loading the skill; the user can still invoke it via the command.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, the team wants a security review subagent that analyzes code for personal data exposure, but that can never edit files or run commands, and that is shared with all developers. What is the best way to configure it?
opcoes: Add to the project's CLAUDE.md: "when acting as a security reviewer, do not edit files or run commands".
Use the built-in general-purpose subagent with a review prompt pasted in by each developer when needed.
Create .claude/agents/lgpd-reviewer.md, version-controlled, with tools: Read, Grep, Glob in the frontmatter.
Create the subagent in each developer's ~/.claude/agents/, with the same tool restrictions.
questoes.explicacao: Custom subagents in .claude/agents/ (version-controlled), with restricted tools in the frontmatter.
feedbacks: A prompt-based restriction is probabilistic; restricting the subagent's tools is deterministic.
general-purpose has broad tool access, and the prompt is not standardized across developers.
Correct. Custom subagents live in .claude/agents/ (shared via git), with tools deterministically restricted in the frontmatter.
Works individually, but is neither shared nor version-controlled; copies diverge over time.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, part of the team uses another coding agent that reads AGENTS.md, and that file already contains all the project conventions. The team wants Claude Code to use the same instructions without maintaining two copies. What is the simplest solution?
opcoes: Create a CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md and adds only what is specific to Claude Code.
Copy the contents of AGENTS.md into CLAUDE.md and create a CI job that alerts when the two diverge.
Rename AGENTS.md to CLAUDE.md, since Claude Code ignores AGENTS.md in every situation.
Keep both files with different content; when both exist, Claude Code merges them automatically.
questoes.explicacao: CLAUDE.md can import AGENTS.md with @AGENTS.md; when both are present, CLAUDE.md wins.
feedbacks: Correct. The @import reuses AGENTS.md as the single source; CLAUDE.md serves as a pointer plus any extras.
Keeps two copies and deals with divergence after it has already happened.
Would break the other agent, and the premise is wrong: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md when there is no CLAUDE.md.
When both exist, CLAUDE.md wins; there is no automatic merging. The clean path is to import.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, a developer investigated a rounding bug on Friday in a long Claude Code session. On Monday, after a large merge that changed several files in the claims module, he wants to continue the investigation. What is the best approach?
opcoes: Use --resume and continue where he left off, since the session history keeps everything that was investigated, including the files read.
A new session with a structured summary of the findings (or --resume while explicitly stating what the merge changed).
Use --fork-session from Friday's session, so that the new line of investigation does not contaminate the original.
Start a new session with no context at all and redo the entire investigation from scratch, so as not to risk bias.
questoes.explicacao: --resume works when the tool results are still valid; if files have changed, start fresh with a structured summary (or state explicitly what changed).
feedbacks: --resume is good when the tool results are still valid; here, the files have changed and the history contains old versions.
Correct. The tool results from the old session (file contents) are stale; a fresh start with a summary, or resuming while flagging what changed, avoids reasoning about old code.
The fork inherits the same stale history; splitting into branches does not fix the staleness.
Wastes the valid findings; the recommended approach is to start fresh with a structured summary, not with nothing.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, after mapping the quoting module in a session, a developer wants to try two alternative refactoring approaches (strategy vs. rules table), building on the understanding already established and without one attempt contaminating the other. What should he do?
opcoes: Continue in the same session, try the first approach, undo the edits, and then try the second.
Open two new sessions from scratch and repeat the mapping in each one.
Create two branches with --fork-session from the mapping session.
Use --resume twice on the same session, in two terminals, one for each approach.
questoes.explicacao: --fork-session creates independent branches from a common base.
feedbacks: The history of the first attempt remains in the context and influences the second: the branches contaminate each other.
Avoids contamination, but wastes the understanding already built.
Correct. --fork-session creates a new ID from a common base: both branches build on the mapping and do not contaminate each other.
Resuming the same ID in parallel mixes the two lines of work in the same history; for independent branches, use fork.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, an internal tool calls the Claude API, sending in every request the tool definitions and a 30,000-token style guide in the system prompt, with cache_control at the end of the system. Even so, usage.cache_read_input_tokens is always zero. The system begins with "Current date and time: 2026-10-11T14:32:07". What is the fix?
opcoes: Move the date/time to after the last breakpoint, leaving the prefix stable.
Add more cache_control breakpoints throughout the style guide to increase the chance of a hit.
Change the cache TTL from 5 minutes to 1 hour.
Move the style guide from the system to the first user message, since messages are cached with priority.
questoes.explicacao: Cache = exact prefix in the order tools → system → messages. Volatile content (timestamps, IDs) goes after the last breakpoint.
feedbacks: Correct. The cache matches an exact prefix; a timestamp at the start of the system changes with every request and invalidates everything that comes after it.
All the breakpoints sit after the timestamp, which has already changed; none of them will match.
A longer TTL does not help when the prefix changes with every request; you still pay the higher write premium.
There is no such priority; the problem is still the volatile content placed before the stable portion.

questoes.pergunta: At Atlas Seguros, after three hours exploring the claims module in a single session, Claude Code started responding with generalities ("this kind of system usually uses typical patterns...") and forgetting discoveries made early on. The investigation still has a long way to go. Which combination of practices is the most advisable?
opcoes: Continue in the same session and ask Claude to "be more specific, cite the code, and don't forget what has already been discovered".
Save findings to a scratchpad file, delegate searches to an Explore subagent, and use /compact proactively.
Open a new session with no summary and restart the exploration of the module from scratch.
Ask Claude to read all of the module's files again to refresh its memory.
questoes.explicacao: Context degradation: a persistent scratchpad, subagents that explore and summarize, proactive /compact with a structured summary.
feedbacks: Does not reduce the accumulated context that causes the degradation; the instruction does not bring back what has already been lost.
Correct. Vague answers and forgetfulness are signs of context degradation; a scratchpad, exploration subagents, and proactive compaction are the mitigations.
Loses all the work done; a fresh start should come with a structured summary or a findings file.
Fills the context even more, worsening the degradation.

questoes.pergunta:
Scenario: Kora Pagamentos, a PIX and card payments fintech, wants to use Claude Code in the GitHub CI pipeline for its monorepo. Plans: (1) automated review of every pull request, whose result blocks the merge and must be delivered within 10 minutes; (2) a nightly analysis of the logs from about 3,000 runs of unstable (flaky) tests; (3) generation of release notes. Constraints: an environment subject to PCI-DSS (the agent may not change anything under infra/pci/ or run arbitrary commands), controlled cost, and outputs that other tools in the pipeline can read automatically.

The first prototype of the review job runs claude "review the changes in this PR" in a GitHub Actions step. The step never finishes and is only terminated by the runner's timeout. What is the most likely cause?
opcoes: --max-turns is missing; the agent went into an infinite loop.
The -p (--print) flag is missing; without it, the interactive session waits for input.
--output-format json is missing, and the runner cannot read the text output.
The runner needs an allocated TTY terminal so that Claude Code can read the repository.
questoes.explicacao: In CI, use -p/--print; without it, the process waits for interactive input.
feedbacks: --max-turns is a useful backstop, but the symptom of hanging with no activity is typical of an interactive session waiting for input.
Correct. -p is the non-interactive mode; without it, the process hangs waiting for the user.
The output format affects parsing of the result; it does not make the process hang.
The CI solution is not to simulate an interactive terminal; it is to use the non-interactive mode (-p).

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, a pipeline script needs to read the review findings (file, line, severity, message) to post comments on the PR. Today, parsing the free-text output breaks frequently. What is the recommended approach?
opcoes: Ask in the prompt to "respond only with valid JSON" and parse the text output.
Use --output-format stream-json and assemble the findings by joining the text chunks from the stream.
Keep the free text and use a second call to Claude to convert the output into JSON.
Use -p with --output-format json and --json-schema with the structure of the findings.
questoes.explicacao: For automated consumption in CI: -p + --output-format json + --json-schema.
feedbacks: Improves the success rate, but does not guarantee schema conformance; parsing still breaks occasionally.
stream-json is for following events in real time; it is still free text to parse, not a guaranteed structure.
Doubles cost and latency and keeps the conversion probabilistic; direct structured output is simpler.
Correct. --output-format json with --json-schema produces structured, validatable output that the pipeline can consume.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the review job needs to read the code, but must not change files, run arbitrary commands, or run indefinitely. Which TWO invocation settings meet this requirement? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: --allowedTools restricted to read-only tools (for example, Read, Grep, and Glob).
--max-turns with a reasonable limit, as a backstop against runaway executions.
--permission-mode bypassPermissions, so that the job does not get stuck waiting for approvals.
The prompt instruction "do not edit files or run commands" as the only restriction.
Run without -p so that an operator manually approves each of the agent's actions during the job.
questoes.explicacao: Restrict tools with --allowedTools/--disallowedTools and use --max-turns as a backstop.
feedbacks: Correct. Deterministically restricts what the agent can do, with no editing and no Bash.
Correct. As a safety ceiling (not as the primary stopping mechanism), it limits the job's time and cost.
Allows everything without asking: exactly the opposite of restricting in a PCI-DSS environment.
A prompt is probabilistic; in a regulated environment, the restriction must be in configuration.
The job would hang waiting for input; human approval of every action does not fit in an automated pipeline.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, to cut costs, someone proposes sending the review of every PR through the Message Batches API, which costs 50% less. The review blocks the merge and must be delivered within 10 minutes. What is the best assessment?
opcoes: Keep the pre-merge review synchronous (Batch has no SLA, up to 24h) and use Batch for the nightly analysis.
Adopt the Batch API for the reviews, since in practice most batches finish within a few minutes.
Adopt the Batch API and, if a result does not arrive within 10 minutes, allow the merge without review.
Adopt the Batch API and use the agent's tool loop inside each request in the batch.
questoes.explicacao: Batch API: 50% cheaper, up to 24h, no SLA, no multi-turn. Never for a blocking CI step.
feedbacks: Correct. Batch is for non-blocking work (nightly reports, bulk processing); a blocking CI step needs predictable latency.
"Most of the time" is not a guarantee: with no SLA, some reviews would delay merges by hours.
Turns a blocking control into an optional one, precisely on the payments code path.
The Batch API does not support a multi-turn tool loop within a request; and the latency problem remains.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the nightly analysis sends 3,000 flaky test logs as a batch to the Batch API. The next morning, the batch finishes with 2,940 requests succeeded, 45 errored, and 15 expired. Which TWO practices are correct? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: Match the results to the tests by their position in the results file, which follows the submission order.
Resubmit the entire batch of 3,000 requests to guarantee a consistent set of results.
Consider the batch failed and fall back to synchronous calls, since there were errors.
Match each result to its source test by custom_id, since results may come back out of submission order.
Resubmit in a new batch only the 60 requests with errored or expired status, identified by custom_id.
questoes.explicacao: Batch: correlate by custom_id (results out of order) and resubmit only the ones that failed.
feedbacks: False premise: results can come back in any order.
Pays again for 2,940 results that are already good, with no gain.
A batch with 98% success is not a failure; just reprocess what did not work.
Correct. Batch results do not follow submission order; custom_id is the correlation key.
Correct. Resubmit only what failed; redoing everything wastes cost and time.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, a 40-file PR that touched the refund flow was reviewed in a single prompt. The review flagged superficial issues in some files, ignored others, and failed to notice that a renamed field in the DTO broke the consumer in another module. Which review structure solves this best?
opcoes: One pass per file with a consistent prompt, plus an integration pass that receives the findings and analyzes cross-module contracts.
Keep a single prompt, but with a larger-window model, so that all 40 files fit comfortably.
Review each file in isolation, with the same prompt for all of them, and publish the combined per-file findings, with no additional step.
Run the same single-prompt review three times and publish the union of the findings.
questoes.explicacao: Large PR: pass 1 per file (consistent prompt) + pass 2 for cross-file integration.
feedbacks: Correct. The per-file pass avoids attention dilution and inconsistency; the integration pass catches cross-file bugs, such as the DTO contract.
Fitting is not the same as getting attention: the problem is attention dilution, not lack of space.
Solves the dilution, but misses the cross-file bug (DTO → consumer), which only shows up in the integration view.
Triples the cost and repeats the same structural blind spot.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the automated review has the categories security, bugs, performance, and style. The style category generates many false positives, and developers have started ignoring all of the bot's comments, including the security ones. What is the most appropriate action?
opcoes: Keep all the categories and add "report only truly important style issues" to the prompt.
Downgrade style comments to the lowest severity, while keeping them posted on the PR.
Disable the style category, refine its criteria with examples, and re-enable it when precision improves.
Require developers to respond to every bot comment before merging, so that none are ignored.
questoes.explicacao: A category with many false positives erodes trust in the others: turn it off, refine the criteria, turn it back on.
feedbacks: "Truly important" is as vague as before; the noise and the loss of trust continue.
The noisy comments keep appearing and eroding trust, just under a different label.
Correct. A noisy category erodes trust in the good ones; turn it off, refine it with explicit criteria, and turn it back on.
Increases friction over bad comments and does not improve precision.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the review findings come out as JSON that always validates against the schema, but about 8% cite line numbers that do not exist in the diff or files that the PR did not change. What is the best fix?
opcoes: Enable strict: true on the schema so that invalid line numbers are rejected.
Validate in code (line in the diff, file in the PR) and retry with the specific errors, with a limit.
Silently discard findings with invalid references and publish the rest.
Resend the same prompt when there is an invalid reference, without stating what was wrong.
questoes.explicacao: Valid schema ≠ semantically correct. Validate in code and retry with the specific errors.
feedbacks: strict guarantees types and fields, not that the line number exists in the diff; that rule must be enforced in code.
Correct. Schema conformance does not guarantee semantic correctness; the validation → specific errors → bounded retry loop solves it.
May throw away real findings that merely have the wrong line, and hides the error rate instead of fixing it.
A blind retry tends to repeat the error; an effective retry feeds back the specific errors.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the team wants to know which types of issues flagged by the review the developers tend to dismiss as irrelevant, in order to tune the prompt based on data. Which change to the review's structured output helps the most?
opcoes: Include in each finding the model's confidence from 0 to 1 and remove findings below 0.6.
Track only the overall rate of findings accepted by developers, week by week.
Include in each finding a detected_pattern field to measure acceptance and dismissal by pattern.
Ask the model to write, at the end of the review, a paragraph about which findings it thinks the developers will ignore.
questoes.explicacao: A detected_pattern field in the output makes it possible to measure, per pattern, what is accepted and what is dismissed.
feedbacks: Self-reported confidence is not calibrated and does not say which patterns are noisy.
An aggregate metric hides which specific patterns cause the dismissals.
Correct. A field that identifies the detected pattern makes it possible to measure the dismissal rate by type and to target the refinement.
The model's speculation is no substitute for measuring the developers' actual behavior.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, a pipeline job uses Claude Code to generate a bug fix and then runs the review with --resume in the same session that generated the fix, "to take advantage of the context". The reviews of these fixes almost never find problems. What should change?
opcoes: Keep --resume and add to the prompt "review with a critical eye, as if you had not written this code".
Use --fork-session from the generation session to do the review in a separate branch.
Increase the review's --max-turns so that it has more time to find problems.
Run the review in a new session, with only the diff and the criteria, without the generation history.
questoes.explicacao: The review should run in an independent session, never in the session that generated the code.
feedbacks: Instructions do not remove the bias of having the generation reasoning in the context.
The fork inherits the entire generation history; the bias comes along with it.
More turns do not fix the context bias; the review still tends to approve.
Correct. The session that wrote the code should not review it: its reasoning context leads it to confirm its own decisions.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the review criteria (e.g., "every log that may contain a card number must use the masker") need to apply both in the CI job and when developers use Claude Code locally, without duplicating text. Where should these criteria go?
opcoes: In --append-system-prompt in the workflow YAML, and ask the developers to paste the same text when using it locally.
In the project's CLAUDE.md (or in .claude/rules/), version-controlled and loaded both locally and in CI.
In each developer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and in the CI runner image.
In a /review skill that developers invoke locally and that the CI job also calls explicitly.
questoes.explicacao: Version-controlled project configuration (CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/) applies equally in local use and in CI with -p.
feedbacks: Duplicates the criteria in two places that will diverge; --append-system-prompt is good for job-specific instructions.
Correct. Version-controlled project configuration applies across all surfaces, including non-interactive mode.
User memory is not shared through the repository; it means multiple copies to maintain.
May work for the review procedure, but criteria that should always apply (including when writing code) belong in the project configuration.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, a CI job asks Claude Code to fix a reconciliation integration test that fails intermittently. The prose description of the expected behavior produced three different fix attempts, all of them rejected. What is the best way to refine the task?
opcoes: Rewrite the prose description with more details and adjectives about the expected behavior.
Give Claude the concrete output of the failing test and iterate by running the tests until they pass.
Switch to a larger model and repeat the same prompt.
Mark the test as skipped in the pipeline until someone has time to investigate manually.
questoes.explicacao: Iterative refinement: failing tests + iterating until they pass beat prose instructions.
feedbacks: Prose remains ambiguous; concrete examples and tests beat descriptions.
Correct. Iterative refinement with tests (TDD): concrete, verifiable failures provide better guidance than prose.
Does not add the concrete information the task is missing.
Hides the problem instead of solving it.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the CI agent may edit code to apply automatic lint fixes, but may never change files under infra/pci/. Today this is stated in the prompt, and in one run the agent changed a configuration file in that folder. What is the appropriate fix?
opcoes: Reinforce the instruction in the prompt with capital letters and an explanation of the PCI-DSS impact.
Add a step at the end of the job that reverts any change in infra/pci/ before the commit.
A PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write that blocks paths under infra/pci/ (exit 2 or deny).
Ask the agent to confirm before each edit that the file is not in infra/pci/.
questoes.explicacao: Compliance rule → PreToolUse hook that blocks in code (exit 2 / deny).
feedbacks: A prompt is probabilistic; it has already failed once and may fail again.
Fixes things after the fact and may fail silently; blocking at the source is simpler and safer.
Correct. A compliance rule needs deterministic enforcement; the hook blocks the action before it executes.
Self-verification by the model is still probabilistic.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, release notes generation always follows the same steps: collect the commits from the previous tag to the current one, classify them (feature, fix, breaking change), draft the notes, and format them using the template. Investigating production incidents, on the other hand, starts without knowing where the problem is. Which decomposition strategy fits each case?
opcoes: Dynamic decomposition for both cases, since it is more flexible and also covers fixed flows.
Prompt chaining for both cases, defining the incident investigation steps in advance.
Prompt chaining for the release notes; dynamic decomposition for the incident investigation.
A single prompt for each case, with no decomposition, to reduce latency.
questoes.explicacao: Prompt chaining for known, fixed steps; dynamic decomposition for open-ended investigation.
feedbacks: Unnecessary flexibility adds cost and unpredictability to a flow that is already known.
Fixed steps do not adapt to what the investigation uncovers; incidents require emergent subtasks.
Correct. Steps known in advance → chaining; open-ended investigation → adaptive decomposition.
Lumps distinct steps into a single prompt, losing control and quality; it ignores the pattern suited to each case.

questoes.pergunta: At Kora Pagamentos, the CI incident analysis agent was connected to three MCP servers (observability, Jira, and a runbook repository) that together expose about 70 tools and more than 25,000 tokens of definitions. Tool selection got worse and each request became more expensive. What is the best approach?
opcoes: Vary the list of tools sent with each request based on the incident's keywords, so that only the relevant ones are sent.
Combine the 70 tools into a single generic execute_action tool with a free-text action parameter.
Keep the 70 tools and increase the model's effort.
Tool search with defer_loading, keeping the 3 to 5 most-used tools non-deferred.
questoes.explicacao: Large catalog / multiple MCP servers → tool search with defer_loading, keeping 3 to 5 frequently used tools non-deferred.
feedbacks: Swapping the tools array on every request invalidates prompt caching and creates a fragile keyword router.
Hides the choice in a schema-less string: it worsens validation, descriptions, and selection.
Does not address the cause (too many tools visible at decision time) and makes it even more expensive.
Correct. With a large catalog and multiple MCP servers, tool search keeps few tools visible at decision time, reduces tokens, and preserves the cache.
